title: skyBlip device configuration (v1)
description: JSON config exchanged over the dedicated GATT characteristic / USB-CDC. The producer (firmware) owns this schema; consumers pin a version. Every key here is read by the firmware: settings with no reader were removed rather than accepted and ignored (region, rotation, power_save, dropped after v1.0; page_mask, dropped when the pad's walk became three pages nothing may hide; stealth and gyro, dropped with the features themselves). Every key is accepted on 'set'; every key but the two per-unit bench trims (battery_offset_mv, frequency_trim_e1_ppm) is also returned by 'get', which is one BLE frame at the 182-byte payload the narrowest phone in the field carries: 166 bytes at its worst case. The radar's range and plot are stored settings with no key here for the same reason: they are set on the device's own menu, and the link neither shows nor sets them. {"command":"defaults"} is answered with command 'defaults' and the keys of 'get' a pilot can set, as a new unit ships them: no version and no address keys, so the reply with its command swapped for 'set' puts a unit back on its defaults; the per-unit trims and the radar's range and plot are not in it and are left as they are.

address.description: The 24-bit ADS-L address this unit transmits under, read-only: manufacturer prefix 0x00 followed by the 16-bit serial skyblip.eu assigned from 1 and signed at activation (activation.v1.schema.json). Absent until the unit is activated, as any key with no reading behind it is: a unit with no serial has no address and neither transmits nor receives, so a page reads 'address' in the reply as activated. Not a stored setting: the unit re-verifies its unlock code at every boot, so a 'set' carrying this key is ignored like any key with no reader

address_mapping_table.description: ADS-L address mapping table (issue 2 F.2.2): 0=random/privacy, 1-4 reserved, 5=ICAO, 6=FLARM, 7=OGN-Tracker, 8=FANET, 9+ manufacturer pages, each a registry-assigned 8-bit prefix and a 16-bit base address. A constant 58 on this device, manufacturer page 49 with prefix 0x00 as the ADS-L registry assigned it, so address is that prefix and the unit's serial. Present whether or not the unit is activated, read-only like address.

alarm_volume.description: 0=off, 1=soft, 2=loud, the three steps of the radar menu's VOLUME row. Off silences the buzzer and the haptic both, as 'alarm_enabled' false does. Soft and loud pulse the haptic with each call. A device ships on loud. Firmware before this scale took 0 to 5, where 3 and up all drove the piezo at the same duty; a stored value comes back as 0 off, 1 and 2 soft, 3 to 5 loud

units.description: 0=nautical (NM, kt), 1=metric (km, km/h): the aeronautical unit is the first one because it is the one a pilot flies, and a device ships on it. Decides every page that prints a distance or a speed: the radar's range ring, the nearby page's distance column, the six-pack's speed dial. Altitudes and vertical speeds stay in feet whatever this says, and the status page shows the aeronautical figure and the SI one side by side

battery_offset_mv.description: Per-unit battery gauge trim in millivolts, added to every reading before a state of charge or a cutoff is read into it. Set once on the production line against a bench supply: two 1% divider resistors put the ratio out by up to 2% (84 mV at a full cell) and the SAADC's gain and reference error adds to that, on a curve whose flat middle spends 250 mV crossing 60 percentage points. The bound is three times the divider's own worst case; beyond it the unit is wired wrong, not out of trim. Write-only over the link: the 'get' reply cannot carry another key (see the top-level description), and the trimmed reading is read back as the millivolts the status reply and the panel already show

frequency_trim_e1_ppm.description: Radio centre-frequency trim in tenths of a ppm, positive upwards, applied to every dwell the SX1262 arms (receive and transmit alike). The board fits a TCXO, so 0 is the design intent and the expected value on every unit; the field exists because nothing on the device can measure the reference, and a batch of TCXOs ten times worse than its datasheet would otherwise be a recall. The bound is that tenfold miss (+-10 ppm, +-8.7 kHz at 868.2 MHz): inside it the carrier cannot leave ERC 70-03 band h1.4 (868.0-868.6 MHz), beyond it the part is broken rather than out of trim. Set only against a spectrum analyser or a frequency counter. Write-only over the link, like battery_offset_mv: the 'get' reply cannot carry another key (see the top-level description), and the device has nothing that could measure the value back for itself.

callsign.description: Upper-case letters, digits, dash and blank, the characters the radar menu types and the ones a $PFLAA ID field can carry, and the aircraft's registration as the radio says it. Set on the radar menu or over this link, shown on the status page, reported back here, and transmitted once every ten seconds: ADS-L's own Traffic payload carries no name, so it goes out under payload type 66, the entry F.2.1 assigns to OGN and whose definition it leaves to them (TelemType 1, InfoType 5, 14 characters). Empty means nothing is transmitted, which is the default and the privacy answer: an address a receiver cannot resolve stays anonymous, and a registration in clear does not. Nine characters here against the wire's fourteen, because that is what the stored settings blob has always held
